The drawing shows an oxazole ring with the following features.

- **Ring:** O1, C2 bearing a phenyl group, N3, C4 (CH), and C5 carrying the side chain.
- **Side chain on C5:** CH2, then CH(Ph), then CH=CH–Ph.
- **Alkene geometry:** the drawing shows a trans (E) double bond, because the phenyl and the CH(Ph) group lie on opposite sides of the zigzag.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH(Ph) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo label.

SMILES for the oxazole: c1ccccc1-c1ncc(o1)CC(c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1

Checking the atoms: the oxazole is o1, c2 (with Ph), n, c4, c5. Written as c2(-Ph)nc(o2)... c5 is bonded to o and to c4, so the ring SMILES c1(Ph)ncc(CC...)o1 is correct.

Final: c1(-c2ccccc2)ncc(CC(c2ccccc2)/C=C/c2ccccc2)o1

SMILES: c1(-c2ccccc2)ncc(CC(c2ccccc2)/C=C/c2ccccc2)o1
